name: bento
title: Bento
description: Tiles of a few sizes fitted into one box, in columns that follow its room.
use: A small set of tiles where some matter more than others: the features of a product, the highlights of a profile, the figures of an overview. The bento counts four, two or one columns from its own width and lets a tile span two columns, two rows or both while there are columns to span. Tiles of one size are an auto grid; tiles of their own heights are masonry.

instead.when: Every tile is the same size and the set grows
Each tile is as tall as what it holds, as in a gallery

platform.fallback: Tiles keep one cell at every width; the columns still follow the room, because they are counted without a query

classes.name: bento
classes.description: The grid: four columns from 48rem of its own width, two from 28rem, one below, and rows at least --bento-row tall. A size container named bento. It draws nothing

classes.name: bento-dense
classes.description: A later tile moves up into a hole an earlier span left. The order seen is no longer the order read, so use it only for a set whose order means nothing

classes.name: bento-wide
classes.description: A tile two columns wide, from 28rem of bento; the whole row in two columns

classes.name: bento-tall
classes.description: A tile two rows tall, from 28rem of bento

classes.name: bento-large
classes.description: A tile two columns wide and two rows tall, from 28rem of bento

classes.name: bento-full
classes.description: A tile across the whole row, at every width

properties.name: --bento-row
properties.description: The least a row may be; a row grows with the tallest thing in it

properties.name: --bento-gap
properties.description: The space between tiles, which the columns are counted with
